ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
July 202 6
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from July 2026 to
Deter Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – The New York City Department of Buildings released its enforcement
bulletin for July 2026, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions to sanction and
deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of safety laws and
codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-imposed disciplinary
actions, including penalties, license suspensions, and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed several major enforcement actions in July, including:
 8 violations and $95,000 in penalties imposed for failure to safeguard
construction sites at 8 locations.
 13 violations and $166,250 in penalties, including daily penalties, imposed for
illegal alterations in 1 location.
 1 violation and $10,000 in penalties issued for failure to perform the duties of a
Construction Superintendent.
 1 padlock closure order issued for violating a stipulation agreement to cease
illegal storage
July’s enforcement efforts also resulted in the removal of 14 illegally parked commercial
trucks and one dead-storage vehicle at two separate locations, and the completion of a
multi-month effort that removed more than 50 commercial trucks and vehicles and 10
shipping containers illegally stored at one location.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for July 2026:
Construction and Design Professionals
 DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited five professionally certified
applications submitted by Registered Architect Jackie Bolalin and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration

Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing
plans that fail to fireproof windows and their assembly in wall on a lot line; failing
to provide two means of egress as required; proposing plans that fail to provide
light and ventilation of the living room through the window; and various other
violations of code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and
Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of
Professional Certification and Directive 14 Final Inspection privileges, which the
Respondent agreed to.
 DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited five professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Shahrish Shuvo and found
major code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications
despite proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require
Alteration Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy;
proposing plans that indicate accessory parking in front of a yard in an zoning
district where this was not permitted; proposing plans that indicate a new
staircase without providing floor framing details; proposing plans that indicate an
interior partition that blocks access to the existing fire escape; and various other
violations of code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and
Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of
Professional Certification and Directive 14 Final Inspection privileges, which the
Respondent agreed to.
 DOB revoked the Special Rigger License of Pritam Singh, after Mr. Singh failed
to ensure a suspended scaffold was being used in a safe and Code compliant
manner at a site where a worker fatally fell. Following an OATH Trial, an
Administrative Law Judge issued a report recommending the revocation of
Singh’s Special Rigger License, which was fulfilled in an order signed by the
DOB Commissioner.
 General Contractor Michael Marino was disciplined for a high number of
sustained Class 1 summonses and for failing to make electronic reports following
incidents. Pursuant to a stipulation, Mr. Marino agreed to a three-month
suspension, a $20,000 fine, and two years of probation
Bronx
 $125,000 in penalties imposed on Hexagon Industries, Inc. for violations
recorded at 57 East Burnside Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after an excavator was used to pull down a wall contrary to the
approved demolition plans, causing the wall to collapse on the sidewalk and
roadway, and damaging a construction fence and sidewalk shed. Violations
included improper demolition, inadequate supervision of the work site, failure to
conduct a pre-shift meeting or to produce site safety orientation records, and lack
of a watchperson on site.

 $20,000 in penalties imposed on AB Builders NY for violations recorded at 1435
Nelson Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the site
after a worker was observed using a single plank and an unstable ladder as a
makeshift platform, and for the supported scaffold that was missing a plank and a
guardrail system. Inspectors also issued violations for Superintendent failing to
perform their duties due to incomplete log records.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Leon D. Matties Const. for violations recorded
at 2075 Webster Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
during concrete barrier repairs after a forklift hit a car in the roadway, and
inspections revealed that the forklift operator lacked the proper training, and that
no flaggers were in place as required during operations.
 Summonses issued to Gammon Enterprizes LLC issued at 461 Park Avenue
South related to a large advertising sign were sustained upon appeal. The
summonses were for work without a permit, owner acting as an Outdoor
Advertising Company (“OAC”) without registration, failure to engage a licensed
sign hanger, failure to post the required UL decal, and for advertising signs
prohibited under the Zoning Resolution. Following the Respondent’s arguments,
the Appeals Board found that the advertising sign’s size had changed
significantly over the years so a legal nonconforming use defense was not
established. The Board also held that the sign being prohibited in a zoning
district is not a defense to a work without a permit charge.
Brooklyn
 $162,250 in penalties imposed on Erez Ephraim Partush for violations recorded
at 945 E 15th Street. DOB issued violations with daily penalties for after observing
the two-family dwelling converted to a 12-family dwelling by the addition of 10
Single Room Occupancies (SROs). Additionally, inspectors issued violations for
lack of automatic sprinklers and Class J fire alarm system as required for
transient use dwellings, and for failure to comply with a previous Vacate Order
issued in 2015.
 $77,350 in penalties imposed on 724 Management LLC for violations recorded at
4402 3rd Ave. DOB inspectors issued administrative code violations for signs on
display without a permit; failure to engage a licensed sign hanger; for the owner
acting as an Outdoor Advertising Company (“OAC”) without registration; and
failure to attach a UL decal. Additionally, Zoning Resolution violations included
prohibited signs within 200 feet and in view of the Gowanus Expressway and
failure to register a sign within 900 feet and in view of an arterial. Violating sign
pictured below.
 $65,210 in penalties imposed on 724 Management LLC for violations recorded at
4404 3rd Ave. DOB inspectors issued Zoning Resolution violations for displaying

an outdoor advertising sign prohibited within 200 feet and in view of the Gowanus
Expressway in an M-1 district; failure to register a sign within 900 feet and in view
of an arterial; and for exceeding height limitations. DOB also issued
administrative code violations for the owner acting as an OAC without
registration, failure to engage a licensed sign hanger, and for failure to attach the
required UL decal. Violating sign pictured below.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on AB Plus R Construction for violations recorded
at 229 Waverly Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard at
a new building job site after observing a lack of guardrails on multiple leading
edges, CMU blocks near a leading edge; and an unsecured metal edge hanging
at one exposure.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Aharon Statfeld for violations recorded at 1770
Kimball Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after
observing a tarp that was deteriorated and not properly secured to the site.
 A Closure Order was executed at 16 Spencer Place following a violation of a
stipulation agreement signed by the property owner to cease use of a
contractor’s yard and commercial vehicle storage in their vacant located in an
R6B residence district. Violating conditions pictured below.

Manhattan
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on CM and Associates Construction for violations
recorded at 38 East 35th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard during excavation operations after observing that a drill went more
than ten feet deep causing a hole in the basement wall of the adjacent building
though excavation plans directed the drill be limited to a six-foot depth.
Queens
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Wang Lam for violations recorded at 185-19
Union Turnpike. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after
observing several uncapped rebars located directly below a working deck area,
creating an unsafe condition for workers.
 Following a padlock warning letter issued for use of a contractor’s yard and
commercial vehicle storage in a vacant lot in an R4 residence district, the owners
of 305 Beach 101st Street signed a stipulation agreement to remove the
commercial trucks and building materials. Violating conditions pictured below.
 The property owners of 305 Cross Bay Boulevard discontinued illegal use of a
contractor’s yard and commercial vehicle storage on their property located in an
R3A residence district following a stipulation agreement where the property
owners agreed to remove a total of 50 commercial trucks and vehicles and 10
commercial shipping containers in stages over the last two years. Corrected
conditions below.

 Following direct outreach, the business owner of 189th Ave, located in a public
right of way owned by the New York City Department of Transportation, removed
14 commercial vehicles illegally stored on the property in an R3A residence
district. Corrected conditions pictured below.
 Following direct outreach, the property owners of 134-33 59th Ave removed the
dead storage of a motor vehicle on their property located in an R4 residence
district. Corrected conditions pictured below.

Staten Island
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on GVC General Contracting for violations
recorded at 154 Hillside Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard the construction site after observing that the rear cellar entry was
accessible to the public during renovations to a fire-damaged 1-family building.
